questions.title: Define an execution error
questions.text: Define the term **execution (runtime) error**.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- An error that occurs while the program is running / executing (the code has no syntax errors) (1)
- an operation cannot be carried out, so the program crashes / stops / shows an error message (1)
scheme.model_answer: An error that happens while the program is running, when an operation such as dividing by zero cannot be carried out, so the program crashes.

questions.title: Type of error

options.content: Logic error that never stops the program

scheme.mark_scheme: B
scheme.explanation: The code translates, but accessing a non-existent element is impossible while running, so it crashes.

questions.title: Runtime errors
questions.text: Select **two** situations that cause an **execution** error.

options.content: Dividing a number by a variable whose value is 0
Misspelling the keyword print as pritn
Converting the input "seven" to an integer
Using > instead of >= in a condition

questions.title: Value causing a runtime error
questions.text:
```python
guess = int(input("Guess a number from 1 to 100: "))
if guess == secret:
    print("Correct!")
```

Give **one** example of a value for `guess` that will cause a runtime error, and explain why.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Example: a string / text, e.g. "Twenty" / "abc" / 3.5 / empty input (1)
- int() cannot convert it to an integer, so the program crashes (ValueError) (1)

points.criterion: Explanation: cannot be converted to an integer

scheme.model_answer: "Twenty" — the int() function cannot convert this text into an integer, so the program stops with a ValueError.

questions.title: Division by zero
questions.text:
The code below crashes when no marks have been entered.

```python
average = total / count
print(average)
```

Rewrite the code so that it does not crash and prints `No marks entered` when `count` is 0.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Checks count before dividing, e.g. IF count > 0 / count != 0 (1)
- performs the division and prints the average in that branch (1)
- ELSE prints "No marks entered" (1)
Accept try/except ZeroDivisionError.

questions.title: Out of range
questions.text:
```text
Scores ← [12, 15, 9, 20, 17]
FOR i ← 0 TO 5
    OUTPUT Scores[i]
ENDFOR
```

Explain why this algorithm causes an execution error and how to correct it.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- The array has indexes 0–4; when i = 5, Scores[5] does not exist — out of range / index out of bounds (1)
- Correct: FOR i ← 0 TO 4 / TO LENGTH(Scores) − 1 (1)
scheme.model_answer: The array has five elements with indexes 0 to 4, so Scores[5] does not exist and causes an out-of-range error. The loop should be FOR i ← 0 TO 4.

questions.title: Preventing a startup error
questions.text: A quiz program opens the file `questions.txt` as soon as it starts. Describe how the programmer can stop the program crashing if the file is missing.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): check that the file exists before opening it; use exception handling (try … except FileNotFoundError); show a clear error message; use default data / ask the user for the file location instead of crashing
scheme.model_answer: The programmer can open the file inside a try … except FileNotFoundError block, and if the file is missing, show the message 'Question file missing' and stop safely instead of crashing.

questions.title: Why test extreme data
questions.text: Explain why a programmer should test a program with **extreme** data.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- To check that values at the boundaries / limits are accepted / processed correctly (1)
- because boundary conditions are often coded wrongly, e.g. < instead of <= (1)

points.criterion: Finds errors in conditions such as < vs <=

scheme.model_answer: To check that the values on the limits of the range are still accepted, because programmers often make mistakes in conditions, such as writing < instead of <=.

questions.title: Why test erroneous data

scheme.mark_scheme:
- To check that invalid data is rejected / the validation works (1)
- so the program does not crash or store / process wrong data; an error message is shown (1)

points.criterion: No crash / wrong data not processed

scheme.model_answer: To check that the program rejects invalid data with an error message instead of crashing or processing wrong values.

questions.title: Validate the input
questions.text: Write pseudocode or program code that asks the user for the number of a month and **keeps asking** until a whole number from 1 to 12 is entered, then outputs `Thank you`.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Input the month (1)
- Loop (WHILE / REPEAT) that repeats while the value is invalid (1)
- Correct condition: < 1 OR > 12 (also checks it is a number, if a language is used) (1)
- Error message / input again inside the loop and output Thank you after it (1)
scheme.model_answer:
INPUT month
WHILE month < 1 OR month > 12 DO
    OUTPUT "Invalid month, try again"
    INPUT month
ENDWHILE
OUTPUT "Thank you"
scheme.ai_instructions: Accept REPEAT … UNTIL month >= 1 AND month <= 12. Accept any language.

questions.title: Testing a cipher function
questions.text:
The function below should shift every lowercase letter of a word to the next letter of the alphabet (a → b, b → c …).

```text
FUNCTION Encrypt(text)
    alphabet ← "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    result ← ""
    text ← lower(text)
    FOR i ← 0 TO LENGTH(text) - 1
        FOR j ← 0 TO 25
            IF text[i] = alphabet[j] THEN
                result ← result + alphabet[j+1]
            ENDIF
        ENDFOR
    ENDFOR
    RETURN result
ENDFUNCTION
```

Note: `lower()` returns the string with all letters in lowercase.

parts.title: Normal data
parts.text: Provide **one** example of normal data for the function.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any text without the letter 'z' (1), e.g. hello
scheme.model_answer: hello

parts.text: Provide **one** example of erroneous data for the function.

scheme.model_answer: buzz

parts.title: Type of error
parts.text: Determine the type of error when `Encrypt()` takes the value `"buZz"` as an argument, and justify your answer.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Runtime error / execution error (1)
Out-of-range array: for z, j = 25 and alphabet[j+1] = alphabet[26] does not exist (1)
scheme.model_answer: Runtime (execution) error. lower() turns Z into z; for z, j = 25, so alphabet[j+1] tries to use index 26, which is outside the array.

scheme.model_answer: y

questions.title: Design a full test plan
questions.text:
A cinema's booking program asks how many seats a customer wants. A customer can book from **1 to 8** seats. The program outputs the total cost at 2 000 tenge per seat, or `Invalid number of seats`.

Write a test plan with **six** tests. For each test give the test data, the type of test data and the expected result. Include all three types of test data.

scheme.mark_scheme:
One mark per correct test (max 5) + 1 mark for including all three types:
- Normal, e.g. 3 → 6 000 tenge; 5 → 10 000
- Extreme: 1 → 2 000; 8 → 16 000
- Erroneous: 0, 9, −2, "two", 2.5 → Invalid number of seats
A test scores only if the data, its type and the expected result are all correct.
scheme.model_answer: 1 Data 3, normal, 6 000 tenge. 2 Data 5, normal, 10 000 tenge. 3 Data 1, extreme, 2 000 tenge. 4 Data 8, extreme, 16 000 tenge. 5 Data 9, erroneous, Invalid number of seats. 6 Data "two", erroneous, Invalid number of seats.

questions.title: A quiz program
questions.text: When a quiz program starts, it reads its questions from the file `quiz.txt` and connects to the school database to save the scores. At the end it calculates `average ← total / count`.

parts.title: Startup error
parts.text: Describe **one** execution error that could occur when the program starts.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Error (1) + description of cause / effect (1), e.g.
- file not found (1): quiz.txt has been deleted / moved, so the program crashes when it tries to open it (1)
- database connection failure (1): the server is not running / wrong password / no network (1)
- access denied (1): no permission to read the file (1)

questions.text:
A program stores the scores of five students and checks new passwords.

```text
Scores ← [12, 15, 9, 20, 17]
FOR i ← 1 TO 5
    OUTPUT Scores[i]

```

Arrays start at index 0. A new password must be **6 to 12 characters** long.

parts.title: Type of error
parts.text: Determine the type of error in the loop and justify your answer.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Runtime / execution error (1)
When i = 5, Scores[5] is outside the array (indexes 0–4) / index out of range (1)
scheme.model_answer: Runtime error, because when i = 5 the program accesses Scores[5], but the array only has indexes 0 to 4.

Extreme: 6 (1) and 12 (1) characters
Erroneous: 5 (1) and 13 (1) characters

parts.title: Why extreme data
parts.text: Explain why the programmer tests the password check with extreme data.

- To check that passwords of exactly 6 and 12 characters are accepted (1)
- because boundary conditions are often written wrongly (e.g. > instead of >=) (1)

summary: Execution (runtime) errors that occur when a program starts or runs and how to prevent them, and testing programs with normal, extreme (boundary) and erroneous data using a test plan.

blocks.content: **Testing** checks that a program **works correctly for every kind of input**, does not crash, and **rejects** data it should not accept. Testing is planned in advance with a **test plan**: for each test, the **test data**, its **type**, the **expected result**, and later the **actual result**.

blocks.title: Kinds of error found by testing
rows: While the program is **starting or running** — it crashes
Division by zero, file not found
The program runs but gives the **wrong result**

blocks.title: More about syntax and logic errors
blocks.content: Syntax and logic errors are studied in the topic **Types of errors**. This topic focuses on **execution errors** and on choosing **test data**.

An error that occurs **while the program is executing**: the code is **syntactically correct**, so it is translated, but an operation **cannot be carried out**, so the program **stops (crashes)** or shows an error message.
Some execution errors happen **as soon as the program starts**, because something the program needs is **missing or unavailable**:

blocks.title: Execution errors at program startup
rows: A configuration or data file that is opened at startup does not exist or has been moved
A library the program needs is not installed or has the wrong version
"The program can't start because xyz.dll is missing" / `ModuleNotFoundError`
The database server is not running, the password is wrong or the network is down
Not enough RAM to load the program or a large array
The user has no right to read a file or write to a folder
The program is started with missing or wrong parameters, or the first input has the wrong type
Another program is using the network port, camera or printer

blocks.title: Execution errors while the program runs
rows: Check the index is within the array bounds
`int("twelve")` when the user types a word for a number
A value too large for its data type
Use a suitable data type; check limits
Make sure recursion has a base case
Using a variable or object that has no value

blocks.content:
guess = int(input("Guess a number from 1 to 100: "))   # user types: Twenty
# ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'Twenty'
blocks.caption: A runtime error caused by input — the program crashes
Preventing startup and input errors with exception handling

blocks.title: Run-time error with an array (exam style)
blocks.content: `Letters` has 26 elements with indexes **0–25**. The code `Letters[j + 1]` is executed when `j = 25`, because the letter **z** has no next letter. Index **26** does not exist, so an **out-of-range (runtime / execution) error** occurs. The fix: when the letter is `z`, use `Letters[0]` (wrap around to `a`).

State the **type** (runtime / execution error) **and justify** it with the **cause** in that code: "*runtime error, because the index j + 1 goes outside the bounds of the array when the input contains z*".
**Typical, valid** data that the program **should accept** and process correctly. It is well **inside** the accepted range and of the correct type and format.

items: Purpose: to check that the program gives the **correct results** for ordinary use.
Choose several normal values, not just one, and work out the **expected result** first.
*Example: a field accepts a month number from 1 to 12 → normal data: 3, 7, 10.*

blocks.content: **Valid** data **at the limits (boundaries)** of the accepted range — the **largest and smallest** values that should still be **accepted**.

items: Purpose: to check that the boundaries are coded correctly — errors such as `<` instead of `<=` are very common.

blocks.title: Boundary testing
blocks.content: Many testers also test the values **just outside** the boundary (0 and 13). These are **erroneous** data — they must be **rejected**. Testing both sides of every boundary is called **boundary testing**.

erroneous | extreme   normal   extreme | erroneous
   ... -1  0    |   1    2 ... 11     12     |   13  14 ...
   -------------+----------------------------+-------------
       rejected |          accepted          | rejected
blocks.caption: Normal, extreme and erroneous data for a range 1–12

blocks.content: Data that **should be rejected** by the program because it is **outside the range**, of the **wrong data type**, in the **wrong format** or **missing**. The program should show an error message and ask again — it must **not crash**.

blocks.caption: Program to be tested: output the season for a month number

blocks.title: Test plan for the season program
How to test a program
items: Read the **validation rule** (range, type, length, format).
Choose **normal** values inside the range, **extreme** values on each boundary and **erroneous** values outside it and of the wrong type.
Write the **expected result** of each test **before** running it.
Run the tests and record the **actual result**.
If the actual result differs, find and correct the error, then **re-test**.

blocks.title: Exam-style answers
blocks.content:
**Q: Give one example of each test data type for a program that accepts a month number. [3]**
Normal: any of 2–11, e.g. **6** (1). Extreme: **1** or **12** (1). Erroneous: **0**, **−15**, **13** or **july** (1).

**Q: Give one example of the value for `guess` that will cause a runtime error. [1]**
A string such as **"Twenty"** — `int()` cannot convert it to an integer.

**Q: The program uses the index of an array element that is outside the bounds of the array indices. State the type of error. [1]**
**Run-time / execution error.**

**Q: Describe one execution error that could occur when the program starts. [2]**
The program tries to open a **settings file that does not exist** (1), so it **crashes with a file-not-found error** unless the error is handled (1).

- Calling extreme data "invalid" — extreme data is **valid** and must be **accepted**.
- Giving erroneous data that is actually valid (e.g. 12 for months 1–12).
- Giving only out-of-range numbers — also test the **wrong data type** (text instead of a number).
- Confusing a **runtime** error (program crashes while running) with a **syntax** error (program cannot be translated).
- Not stating the **expected result** in a test plan.
